name: Mummy Mountain
generated_description:
Mummy Mountain is a 11,332-foot summit in Nevada. The Mummy Mountain Trail covers 0.6 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 180 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

Along the way the route passes a spring (Mummy Spring) near mile 0.32 — useful checkpoints for judging your pace.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 36.29398, -115.63376 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 30 miles west of Las Vegas, Nevada. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

The reliable snow-free window is roughly July through September. At this elevation, afternoon thunderstorms are a serious summer hazard — start early and plan to be off the upper mountain by midday. Outside that window expect snow travel and bring traction and navigation skills to match.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Charleston Peak and Griffith Peak — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.answer: Mummy Mountain stands at 11,332 feet (3,454 meters) in Nevada.
